Do not place the console or power supply near any heat sources, such as radiators, heat registers, stoves, or amplifiers.

This test verifies that you can stream music and photos to your console from a Computer. If your console does not pass this test:
Verify that your computer is connected and powered on.

Make sure that Windows Media Connect is running on the computer, and that sharing with your console has been enabled. On your computer, click Start, click Control Panel, and then double-click Windows Media Connect. If you do not have Windows Media Connect installed, go to www.xbox.com/pcsetup to install it.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/media or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test detects your network adapter and verifies that it is physically connected.  If you are using a wired-only connection, this test verifies that an Ethernet cable is connected to your console's Ethernet port.  If you are using an Ethernet-to-wireless bridge, this test verifies that your console can communicate with your wireless bridge.  If you are using the Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter, this test verifies that your adapter is properly connected to your console.
Note: The Xbox 360 Wireless Network Adapter is disabled while an Ethernet cable is plugged into your console's Ethernet port.
If you are using a wired-only connection and the test reports Disconnected:
Check that the Ethernet cable is not damaged and is connected to the console's Ethernet port.
Verify that the device you are connecting to your console (modem, router, or gateway) is connected and powered on.
If you are using an Ethernet-to-wireless bridge and the test reports Wired or Disconnected:
Verify that your Ethernet-to-wireless bridge is powered on.
Check that the Ethernet cable to your bridge is not damaged and is connected to the console's Ethernet port.
If you are using the Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter and the test reports Wired or Wireless Bridge:
The Ethernet port is being used instead of the wireless adapter.  Disconnect the Ethernet cable to use the wireless adapter.
If you are using the Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter and the test reports Disconnected:
Verify that your wireless adapter is connected directly to the rear panel USB port. Do not connect your wireless adapter to a USB hub.
Make sure that there is adequate ventilation around the wireless adapter.
Disconnect then reconnect your wireless adapter, then turn your console off and back on.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
This test verifies that the wireless adapter connected to your console is connected to a wireless network.  If your console does not pass this test:
If you are using an Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter, verify that an Ethernet cable is NOT plugged into your console's Ethernet port.
Verify that your wireless access point, gateway, or router is powered on.
Remove any obstructions between your Xbox 360 console and your wireless access point.
Turn off any devices that may interfere with your wireless network (for example, microwave ovens or 2.4-GHz telephones).

If you are using an infrastructure network, make sure the security settings on your wireless adapter match those on your wireless access point, gateway, or router (for example, your WEP key or WPA passphrase must match).
If you are establishing an ad-hoc network, make sure the network name, channel, band and security settings match the settings on the device you are establishing a connection with.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
This test verifies that your console has a valid IP address. If your console does not pass this test:
Confirm that there are no other devices on your network with the same IP address.
If you are using a router or gateway, verify that it is configured to assign IP addresses to network devices (DHCP enabled).
If you are connecting to a router, make sure that your console's Ethernet cable is not connected to the WAN port of the router.

If you are connecting directly to a modem, and your ISP requires PPPoE settings, verify that your PPPoE user name and password are correct. If PPPoE credentials are not required by your ISP, remove the PPPoE user name and password settings.

If you are connecting directly to a modem and have replaced a device that was connected to your modem with your console or another device, turn the modem off and back on before connecting the new device.
If you are using a static IP address from your ISP, contact your ISP to verify the address.

If your console is connected to an ad-hoc network, it will probably not pass this test. If your IP address is assigned automatically and your ad-hoc network does not include a DHCP server, this does not indicate a problem. The test is properly reporting that a DHCP server could not be contacted.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
This test verifies that your console can contact your ISP's DNS servers. If your console does not pass this test:
Verify that your console has passed the IP Confirmed test. If your IP address is not confirmed, your console cannot pass the DNS test.
If your IP address is confirmed and you are using a router or gateway, make sure that you can browse the Web from a computer on the same router or gateway that your console is using.
If you are connecting directly to a modem, verify that you have entered the correct DNS server settings. You can get your DNS server settings from your Internet service provider (ISP).
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test confirms that your network has a sufficient Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU). MTU is a setting on your router or gateway that can affect network performance. Xbox Live requires a minimum MTU setting of 1364. If your console does not pass this test, you will not be able to sign in to Xbox Live. See your router or gateway instruction manual for information about changing the MTU setting.
If you change your MTU setting and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test evaluates how your router or gateway will respond to a particular type of Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) packet. If your network fails this test, you will not be able to sign in to Xbox Live. To fix, remove the router or gateway from your network or replace it with an Xbox Live Compatible router or gateway. For a listing of devices that have earned this certification, go to www.xbox.com.
If you've tried this suggestion and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test verifies that your console can contact Xbox Live. If your console does not pass this test, check your IP Confirmed, DNS Verified, MTU, and ICMP tests. A failure on any of these tests will prevent you from signing in to Xbox Live. If your console passes all of these tests and still cannot sign in to Xbox Live, verify that your account information is accurate and up to date.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test indicates the type of Network Address Translation (NAT) that your router or gateway is using. Devices that perform strict or moderate NAT can limit the ability of gamers to find each other, participate in sessions, or hear each other on Xbox Live.

You will not receive a result for this test if you are unable to sign in to Xbox Live. If you do not receive a result, test your connection to Xbox Live. If your router or gateway is using a moderate or strict NAT, replace it with an Xbox Live Compatible device. For a listing of devices that have earned this certification, see www.xbox.com.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

Questo test conferma che la rete abbia una sufficiente unit
massima di trasmissione (Maximum Transmission Unit, MTU). MTU

un'impostazione sul router o sul gateway in grado di influenzare le prestazioni della rete. Xbox Live richiede un'impostazione MTU minima di 1364. Se la console non supera questo test, non sarai in grado di connetterti a Xbox Live. Questo test valuta se il router o il gateway risponder

ad un particolare tipo di pacchetto del protocollo dei messaggi di controllo Internet (Internet Control Message Protocol, ICMP). Se la rete non supera questo test, non sarai in grado di connetterti a Xbox Live. Per risolvere questo problema, rimuovi il router o il gateway dalla rete o sostituiscilo con un router o con un gateway compatibile con Xbox Live. Per un elenco di periferiche che hanno ottenuto questa certificazione, visita il sito www.xbox.com.
Se hai provato questo suggerimento e la console continua a non superare questo test, vai a www.xbox.com/setup o chiama il Supporto clienti Xbox.

Se la console supera tutti questi test e non sei ancora in grado di connetterti a Xbox Live, verifica che le informazioni del tuo account siano accurate e aggiornate.
Se hai provato questi suggerimenti e la console continua a non superare questo test, vai a www.xbox.com/setup o chiama il Supporto clienti Xbox.

Go to Xbox Live Marketplace add Microsoft Points to your account.

Points that you purchase never expire. Points that are awarded to you through promotions can have expiration dates for the promotion. To view the information about expiration dates for your points, go to https://billing.microsoft.com and log in with your Passport Network account.

Manage approval of your child's online friends.
Other people on Xbox Live may want to add your child to their personal friends list. You can require these requests to be approved by you, or you can allow your child to approve them on their own.

Select Require Approval to require that all new friend requests be approved by you. You must also approve any new friend requests that your child wants to send to other people. Select Approval Not Required to allow your child to send and accept new friend requests on their own.

Everyone on Xbox Live has a friends list that connects them with other gamers they like to play with. When an Xbox Live member adds someone to their friends list, that person receives a new friend request, which they can accept or reject.
Use New Online Friends in Family Settings to keep your child from sending or accepting friend requests without your permission. To approve requests, you must enter your Passport Network password.
Some Family Settings have a Friends Only option. If you use this option to approve friend requests, your child will be able to interact only with people that you have approved.
Control who your child is allowed to communicate with on Xbox Live.
Communication on Xbox Live includes chat, messages, and game invites using voice, video, or text.

Select Everyone to allow your child to communicate with anyone on Xbox Live. Select Friends Only to allow your child to communicate only with people on their friends list. Select Blocked to block everyone from communicating with your child. Your child will still receive new friend requests.
Use privacy and friends settings to determine how your child appears to and interacts with people on Xbox Live.
New Online Friends: Decide whether to approve all new friend requests, or allow your child to send and receive friend requests on their own.
Communications: Decide who your child communicates with.
Gamer Profile Sharing: Decide who can see your child's gamer profile information.
Gamer Profile Viewing: Decide whose profiles your child is allowed to see.
Online Status: Decide who can see your child's online status and activity information.
Decide whether other people can see your child's online status.
If you allow others to see your child's online status, they can see your child's current online activity, such as the game they are playing and whether they are available to play a game.

Select Everyone to allow everyone on Xbox Live to see your child's online status and current activity. Select Friends Only to allow only your child's friends to see your child's online status and current activity. Select Blocked to block everyone from seeing your child's online status and current activity.
Decide who can see your child's gamer profile.
Your child's gamer profile includes their motto and information about their online achievements and game history.

Select Everyone to allow everyone on Xbox Live to see your child's gamer profile. Select Friends Only to allow only your child's friends to see your child's gamer profile. Select Blocked to block everyone from seeing your child's gamer profile.
Decide whether your child can see other people's gamer profiles.
A gamer profile includes information about a member's online achievements and game history. It can also contain a gamer's motto, which may be inappropriate for children.

Select Everyone to allow your child to see everyone's gamer profile. Select Friends Only to allow your child to see only the gamer profiles belonging to your child's friends. Select Blocked to block your child from seeing anyone's gamer profile.

Your rep is your reputation on Xbox LIVE. It is a snapshot of how other players see you. Rep is determined by player reviews submitted about you. A high rep means other players like to play with you, and a low rep means many players want to avoid you. Your rep changes as other players submit player reviews about you. You can see information about your reviews on your gamer card.

When you avoid a player, you become less likely to be matched with that person in the future. This may also affect that player's rep. When you prefer a player, you become more likely to be matched with that person in the future. This may also affect that player's rep. You can change your review of a player by submitting a different review. Changing your review will not affect the player's rep.
